title: Emergency capacity arbitration and nonlinear autoscale safeguards
creator: Elena Park
description:
Summary: During the last two dedicated-pool incidents we observed nonlinear failures in the autoscaler: pools oscillated, headroom drained unexpectedly, and tenant-level fairness caused noisy neighbors to starve critical workloads. This ticket authors a mitigation RFC and implements an operational arbitration layer that sits between the autoscaler and fleet controller to preserve throughput guarantees while avoiding cascading scale regressions.

Goals:
- Define an emergency arbitration policy that enforces minimum per-tenant headroom and nonlinear backoff thresholds.
- Implement a lightweight admission/adjudication service (in front of the autoscaler) that can temporarily hold scale decisions and apply canary throttles or prioritized allocations.
- Add observability and runbook updates that allow SREs to detect, manually override, and validate arbitration actions.
- Produce postmortem action items and a migration plan to replace brittle heuristics in the existing autoscaler with a measured, predictable policy.

Non-goals: full rewrite of the autoscaler runtime; replacing capacity planning tooling (this ticket is focused on incident mitigation and short-medium term resilience).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Arbitration service can intercept and delay up to 80% of aggressive scale-downs for 120s and apply canary throttles for new scale-ups. 2) Integration tests exercising a synthetic noisy-tenant load show <5% SLA breach vs current ~22% during identical surge. 3) Runbook pages updated with play-by-play recovery steps and manual overrides. 4) Postmortem action items mapped to owner and milestone in backlog.

Create integration test that replays production surge pattern (load-testing)

comments: 2026-03-01 Elena Park: Created ticket after post-incident review on 2026-02-28. Primary concern: oscillation around scale boundaries and lack of per-tenant minimum headroom. Reference: internal incident notes and timeline.

2026-03-03 Marcus Li: PoC admission controller running locally. It intercepts scaler decisions and can apply an explicit 'hold' for a configurable window. Early tests show we can prevent 1/3 of rapid scale-downs without increasing overall costs in short windows.

2026-03-05 SRE Team Lead (Priya Nair): Requested ability to manually set arbitration overrides via console; flagged audit-log requirements for compliance. Priya -> created follow-up PM ticket for console controls.

2026-03-07 Elena Park: RFC v0.1 posted to Confluence: confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Arbitration-RFC. Key trade-offs documented: delaying scale-down reduces short-term cost savings but preserves tail latency; adding admission layer increases decision path complexity and needs high-availability deployment.

2026-03-09 Marcus Li: Integration test results uploaded: grafana.redwood.ai/d/scale-tests/dedicated-arbitration (compare baseline vs arbitration). Observed 45% reduction in 99th percentile latency spikes under noisy neighbor workload during 60s surges.

2026-03-11 PM Review (Jasper O'Neill): Approved prioritization for P0; requested clear rollback plan and cost accounting for arbitration windows. Also requested that policy be parameterized per-customer (enterprise customers may opt-out).

2026-03-12 Security (Ayesha Khan): Reviewed audit/log schema and asked for explicit KMS-scoped keys for arbitration audit store. Assigned to infra team. Will require follow-up before enterprise rollout.

2026-03-13 Marcus Li: Implemented canary deploy in pool 'dedicated-eu-west-2a-3' with 2-hour observation window; results look good (no regressions). Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234 for review.

Complete security KMS integration for audit logs (Infra)
